rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;

SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: Assuming "most albums" means the count of rows in Album per artist, with ties all shown.

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC, Country;
rows.note: Assuming each row in Customer is one customer and NULL countries should be shown as their own group.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assumption: total revenue per year is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by the year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assuming "total amount spent" means the sum of Invoice.Total per customer.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: "support rep" means the Employee referenced by Customer.SupportRepId, and I'll count distinct customers per rep.

rows.sql: SELECT p.Name, COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS TrackCount FROM Playlist p LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge' GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId);
rows.note: Assuming "purchased" means the track appears in any InvoiceLine, I'll count tracks with no matching InvoiceLine.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming revenue means the sum of invoice Total grouped by BillingCountry for invoices dated in 2012.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.Name FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3 ORDER BY ar.Name LIMIT 50
rows.note: Assumption: an artist's tracks are linked through Track → Album → Artist, and genres are counted as distinct GenreId values.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is computed from InvoiceLine (UnitPrice × Quantity) grouped by track genre, with each genre's share of the overall line-item total.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
  AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
    SELECT i2.CustomerId
    FROM Invoice i2
    JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
    JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
    JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
    WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
  );
rows.note: I'm assuming the genre names are exactly 'Rock' and 'Jazz', and that a purchase is any invoice line linked to a track of that genre.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT Discontinued, COUNT(*) AS ProductCount FROM Products GROUP BY Discontinued;
SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany' LIMIT 50

SELECT c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY ProductCount DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT substr(OrderDate, 1, 4) AS OrderYear, COUNT(*) AS NumOrders FROM Orders GROUP BY OrderYear ORDER BY OrderYear
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName
rows.note: Assuming "shipper" means the ShipVia shipper on each order, I'll average Orders.Freight grouped by the shipper's company name.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')

SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID WHERE o.OrderDate LIKE '2020%' GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName ORDER BY OrderCount DESC LIMIT 1;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS ProductsAboveAverage FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" means the simple average of UnitPrice across all products in the Products table.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrdersShippedToFrance FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';

SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: revenue per line is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), summed per product.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice
FROM Products p
JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
WHERE p.UnitPrice = (
  SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
)
ORDER BY c.CategoryName;

SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue FROM Orders o JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: I'm assuming OrderDate is a date/datetime string and that "2021" means calendar year 2021.

rows.sql: SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '1997-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '1998-01-01' GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName ORDER BY OrderCount DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: The database has no orders dated in 1997. The Orders table has 16,282 rows with OrderDate values from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, and none fall in 1997, so no employee can be identified for that year. If you meant a different year in that range, I can run the same count for it.
